      <title>Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/24/chelsea-tottenham-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game.</p><p>Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/24/chelsea-tottenham-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>
